# Determining if Students Should do More Programming Practice

This analysis compared the results of 3 different survey answers. The first chart explores the overall effectiveness of practice programming. The second chart depicts the overall effectiveness of ls questions. The last two charts each compare the resuls of the first two charts with the overall student preparedness of quizes. The goal of these charts is to determine if there is any correlation between the two different practice types, student preference, and quiz preparedness.

## Conclusion
The idea I was trying test was whether this class should include more programming exercises because they would better aid students to prepare for quizzes. I included a graph to see how students viewed the effectiveness of programming practice. I then did the same to see how students viewed the effectiveness of ls questions, so I can compare the effectiveness of the two assignment types. I then used a helper function of my own design to isolate students with the least coding experience to determine if their results for programming effectiveness differed. Next, I compared programming effectivesness with quiz preparation to see if there was a correlation between the two. Finally I did the same with ls questoins to once again compare the two assignment types. 

Overall, my analysis found that students believe programming effectiveness was exettremely helpful, with the vast majority of students selecting 5-7. However, the ls quetions had very similar results with the vast majority being between 5-7. However, there were more overall 6s and 7s for programming efectiveness. In addition, I found that students who believed the ls questions and coding practice were helpful also found themselves more prepared for quizes. However positive these results are, I believe they led to inconclusive data because the asnwers between ls and programming are too similar. It is very difficult to find an advantage of one over the other, leading me to think that the current method for practice is effective. I believe an additional question stating "I believe programming practice is more effective at preparing me for quizes than ls questions" would benefit this analysis. This provides direct evidence to either support or refute my claim. The only negative tradeoff I see with my idea is it utilizes more of students time. Obviously, coding practice takes much more time than completing ls questions. However, this is a trade off for more effective learning and hands on experience with python. In addition, by decreasing the number of ls questions, students can spend more time practicing programming. I also believe these assignments can have more flexibility, allowing students to do coding projects that relate to their major, helping to prepare students for using coding in their future academic or professional careers.
